messages.subject: F-statistic in Lavaan
parts:
Hi there,
I am running an SEM model with a categorical exogenous variable (5 nominal categories not ordinal) in lavaan. Is there a way I could get F-statistic in addition to z/t-statistics? I was also wondering if there is a way to run such a model at once with different reference categories so as to tell how each category differs from others, kind of similar to pairwise comparisons in ANOVA. I am trying to avoid running the model multiple times by alternating the reference category.
Thank you in advance for your help.
Pita

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: F-statistic in Lavaan
parts:
Instead of getting an F statistic, you can get a chi-square statistic, which will do the same thing.

You can do this  by constraining all the values to be equal in the model, and using a chi-square difference test.

One thing I like to do, to make sure I've understood this sort of thing, is to run a model that I understand using regression, and then run the same regression model in lavaan to ensure I get the same result. Then I move to the model with latent variables.

Jeremy

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: F-statistic in Lavaan
parts: Hi Peter

On Mon, 10 Feb 2020 at 15:32, Peter MKUMBO <pmk...@g.clemson.edu> wrote:
Thank you Jeremy for your response. I meant omnibus F-statistic for that particular "regression model" with nominal categorical predictors.

That's what I meant too. :)  

Here's an example of what I was talking about. 
set.seed(1234)

library(dplyr)

d <- data.frame(x = sample(1:5, 1000, TRUE))
d$y <- rnorm(1000) + d$x * 0.1

fit1 <- lm(y ~ factor(x), data = d)
summary(fit1)
anova(fit1)

d <- d %>%
  dplyr::mutate(x1 = x == 1,
                x2 = x == 2,
                x3 = x == 3,
                x4 = x == 4,
                x5 = x == 5)

library(lavaan)

model2 <- "
 y ~  x2 +  x3 + x4 + x5
 y ~~ y
 y ~ 1 "

fit2 <- lavaan::sem(model2, data = d)
summary(fit2)

model2a <- "
 y ~ b1 * x2 + b2 * x3 + b3 * x4 + b4 * x5
 y ~~ y
 b1 == 0
 b2 == 0
 b3 == 0
 b4 == 0"
fit2a <- lavaan::sem(model2a, data = d)
summary(fit2a)


The omnibus F test gives a p-value of 0.017. The parameter estimates in fit2 match the parameter estimates in fit1.

The fit2a chi-square test in the final model gives a p-value of 0.017, which is the same as the anova for fit1.
